ei.title: A Journey From War to the Olympics
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to represent Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true.

However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war. If they reached Europe, the rest of the family would follow. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to pursue her dream and live without fear.

In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to reflect. She had to take action immediately in order to save herself and the other passengers. She jumped into the water along with Sara and two others, and the four of them guided the drifting boat. They swam for three and a half hours until they arrived safely with all the other passengers on the shore of a Greek island.

Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land.

She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.

Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.

At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was determined to pour everything she had into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter. In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a statement, she remarked, "I want everyone to stay strong for their goals in life, because if you have your goals in front of your eyes, you will do everything you can; and I think even if I fail, I will try again. ... I want to show everybody that it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it; everyone can do it."

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ to watch → watching: enjoy는 동명사를 목적어로 취함
det.analysis:
✅ ① growing: 현재분사. a girl growing up 적절
✅ ② centered: 과거형. her life centered around 적절
❌ ③ to watch → watching: enjoy + V-ing(동명사). to부정사 불가 ← 정답
✅ ④ to represent: got the chance to V. to부정사 적절
det.tip: enjoy + V-ing: 동명사만 목적어로 취하는 동사. enjoy watching(O), enjoy to watch(X).

questions.passage: At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① stepping → stepped: When절의 동사는 과거형 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① stepping → stepped: When she stepped onto. 시간 부사절 동사는 과거형 ← 정답
✅ ② determined: was determined to V. be determined to 구문 적절
✅ ③ proud: was proud to have made. be동사 + 형용사보어 적절
✅ ④ matter: did not matter. 부정문 동사원형 적절
det.tip: When + S + V(과거형): 시간 부사절. stepping(현재분사)은 부사절 동사 불가.

det.korean: ④ grown → grew: grow의 과거형 grew 필요. grown은 과거분사
det.analysis:
✅ ① reached: 조건절 과거형. If they reached → would follow. 가정법 과거 적절
✅ ② making: 전치사 by + 동명사 적절
✅ ③ designed: 과거분사. a boat designed for 수식 적절
❌ ④ grown → grew: 과거형 필요. grew worse(더 나빠졌다). grown은 과거분사(have grown 형태 필요) ← 정답
det.tip: grow - grew - grown: 과거형 grew, 과거분사 grown. 단독 서술어에는 과거형 grew 사용.

questions.passage: Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to ①<u>reflect</u>. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ abandoned → guided: 표류하는 보트를 '버린' 것이 아니라 '안내한' 것
det.analysis:
✅ ① reflect(숙고하다): 원문 일치. 숙고할 시간이 없었다
✅ ② save(구하다): 원문 일치
❌ ③ abandoned(버리다) → guided(안내하다): 4명이 보트를 안내하여 그리스 섬에 도착 ← 정답
✅ ④ safely(안전하게): 원문 일치
det.tip: guided = 안내하다. abandoned = 버리다. 보트를 버린 게 아니라 끌고 갔다.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ prolong → avoid: 전쟁을 '연장하러' 간 것이 아니라 '피하려고' 독일로 간 것
det.analysis:
✅ ① risky(위험한): 원문 일치. 평범한 활동이 위험해짐
✅ ② clung(매달렸다): 원문 일치. 꿈을 놓지 않았다
✅ ③ wake-up call(경각심): 원문 일치
❌ ④ prolong(연장하다) → avoid(피하다): 전쟁을 피하기 위해 독일로 간 것 ← 정답
det.tip: avoid = 피하다. prolong = 연장하다. 전쟁을 연장하러 간 게 아니라 피하러 간 것.

questions.passage: The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 즉시 행동에 나서야(take action) 했다
det.analysis:
✅ ① take action(행동에 나서다): immediately와 자연스럽게 연결. 물에 뛰어든 행동과 일치 ← 정답

❌ ② call for help(도움 요청): 직접 물에 뛰어들어 행동했으므로 부적절

❌ ③ give up hope(희망 포기): 결국 모두 구했으므로 포기와 모순

❌ ④ wait patiently(참을성 있게 기다리다): immediately와 정반대
det.tip: take action = 행동에 나서다. jumped into the water가 구체적 행동.

questions.passage: She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to __________. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 탁월함을 추구하는(pursue excellence) 노력
det.analysis:
✅ ② pursue excellence(탁월함 추구): 집중과 끈기로 노력하는 맥락. 원문 일치 ← 정답

❌ ① avoid challenges(도전 회피): 적극적 노력과 모순

❌ ③ gain fame(명성 획득): 문맥에 명성 언급 없음

❌ ④ reject criticism(비판 거부): 코치 지도를 따르는 맥락과 불일치
det.tip: pursue excellence = 탁월함을 추구하다. stay focused and persistent가 단서.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. ch: 시리아 내전으로 학교 가는 것이 위험해졌다

det.korean: ③ 시리아 내전으로 학교 가는 것이 위험해졌다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 2015년: 원문 2011년. 연도 오류
❌ ② 폭발: 원문 'did not explode' 폭발하지 않았음
✅ ③ 학교 위험: 'normal activities like going to school became risky' ← 정답
❌ ④ 형제자매 없음: 원문에 sister Sara 존재
det.tip: 2011년 내전 발발. 폭탄은 폭발하지 않았다(did not explode).

ch: 때때로 작은 차와 붐비는 버스를 이용했다
자매는 마케도니아, 세르비아, 헝가리, 오스트리아를 거쳤다

det.korean: ① 30일 → 원문은 25일(25-day journey)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 30일: 원문 '25-day journey'. 25일이 맞으므로 불일치 ← 정답
❌ ② 차와 버스: 원문 'caught rides in small cars and crowded buses' 일치
❌ ③ 4개국: 원문 일치
❌ ④ 베를린 난민 센터: 원문 일치
det.tip: 25-day journey = 25일간의 여정. 30일이 아님.

ch: Yusra의 아버지는 전직 프로 수영 선수였다
Yusra는 올림픽 수영 경기를 혼자서 시청했다
Yusra는 어린 나이에 수영을 배우기 시작했다

det.korean: ② 혼자 시청 → 원문: 아버지와 함께(with her father) 시청
det.analysis:
❌ ① 전직 프로: 원문 'former professional swimmer' 일치
✅ ② 혼자 시청: 원문 'with her father'. 혼자가 아님 ← 정답(불일치)
❌ ③ 어린 나이: 원문 'from a young age' 일치
❌ ④ 특별한 재능: 원문 'special talent' 일치
det.tip: with her father = 아버지와 함께. 혼자(alone)가 아님.

난민 보호를 위한 국제 사회의 노력
육로 여행과 해상 여행의 장단점 비교

det.korean: 위기 상황에서 포기하지 않는 끈기와 행동력
det.analysis:
✅ ① 끈기와 행동력: 물에 뛰어들어 보트를 이끌고, 25일간 포기하지 않고 이동 ← 정답

❌ ② 안전 수칙: 안전 수칙 언급 없음

❌ ③ 국제 사회: 국제 지원 관련 내용 없음

❌ ④ 장단점 비교: 비교 분석이 아닌 서사
det.tip: 핵심: kept moving, guided the boat — 포기하지 않는 행동의 연속.

questions.stem: Yusra의 인터뷰 발언에서 추론할 수 있는 핵심 메시지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Winning medals is the ultimate measure of success in sports
Dreams are achievable through persistence despite failures and hardships
Refugee athletes deserve more support from international organizations
Physical strength matters more than mental determination in competition

det.korean:
② Dreams are achievable through persistence despite failures and hardships
(실패와 역경에도 불구하고 끈기를 통해 꿈은 이룰 수 있다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① Winning medals is the ultimate measure of success in sports (스포츠에서 메달을 따는 것이 성공의 궁극적 척도이다)
→ 본문: 'The time on the scoreboard did not matter.' 기록보다 참여의 의미 강조. 모순.

✅ ② Dreams are achievable through persistence despite failures and hardships (실패와 역경에도 불구하고 끈기를 통해 꿈은 이룰 수 있다)
→ 본문: 'it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible', 'even if I fail, I will try again' ← 정답

❌ ③ Refugee athletes deserve more support from international organizations (난민 선수들은 국제기구의 더 많은 지원을 받을 자격이 있다)
→ 인터뷰에서 지원 요청 없음

❌ ④ Physical strength matters more than mental determination in competition (경쟁에서 정신력보다 체력이 더 중요하다)
→ 본문: 'stay strong for their goals'. 정신력의 중요성 강조. 반대.
det.tip: 핵심 문장: 'it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it.'

questions.passage: Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be <u>a wake-up call</u> for Yusra and her sister Sara. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 a wake-up call이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: A daily routine that keeps one motivated and energized
A shocking event that forces one to recognize a serious situation
A telephone call that interrupts sleep in the early morning
A comforting message from a trusted friend during a crisis

det.korean:
② A shocking event that forces one to recognize a serious situation
(심각한 상황을 깨닫게 하는 충격적 사건)
det.analysis:
❌ ① A daily routine that keeps one motivated and energized (동기 부여를 하는 일상)
→ 일상이 아닌 폭탄 사건이라는 충격적 사건

✅ ② A shocking event that forces one to recognize a serious situation (심각한 상황을 깨닫게 하는 충격적 사건)
→ 본문: 폭탄 사건 후 '더 이상 머물 수 없다'고 깨달음. 비유적 의미 ← 정답

❌ ③ A telephone call that interrupts sleep in the early morning (아침에 잠을 깨우는 전화)
→ 문자 그대로의 의미. 비유적 해석 필요

❌ ④ A comforting message from a trusted friend during a crisis (위기 중 친구의 위로 메시지)
→ 위안이 아닌 경각심의 계기
det.tip: wake-up call = 경각심을 일깨우는 사건(비유). 문자 의미(기상 전화)가 아닌 비유적 의미.

In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land. She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to <u>do so</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 do so가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: do so = 그녀의 코치가 되어 주는 것
det.analysis:

questions.passage: Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day. Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although <u>it</u> seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: it = 난민 팀에 합류하라는 초대

✅ ② 난민 팀 초대: 'was invited to join the refugee team' → 'it seemed like a great opportunity' ← 정답

❌ ③ 수영 훈련 재개: 이전 문단 내용

❌ ④ 귀국: 피난 중이므로 부적절
det.tip: it = 앞 문장의 명사구. 'was invited to join the refugee team' → it(그 초대).

questions.passage: When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to represent Syria in an international swimming championship.

questions.passage: In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.
